newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude prices hit hard on API sell-off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude prices hit hard on API sell-off.

text.p: U.S. cash crude markets started Wednesday in a weak state, pushed to lower prices following release of bearish industry and U.S. Department of Energy stock reports.

June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing traded 35 cents weaker at $20.95-21.05 in mid-morning activity. The market's week-long flirtation with backwardation folded, as June WTI lost its premium to July in a move back to contango.

Usually crude markets find prompt contracts trading at stronger prices than months that follow, putting prices in backwardation. But recent market bearishness has put June WTI on the defensive at a discount to July, a condition that only lifted briefly from late last week when fundamental supply concerns boosted June's performance.
On Wednesday, domestic grade barrels failed to excite much activity with deals steady to weaker from Tuesday.
Cash crude traders said markets were lightly attended due to a confluence of industry functions.
"It's a little bare out there, with not much moving," said a Texas dealer.

Confirmed trades had Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at a six cents premium to the June/WTI, four cents lower that Tuesday. Softer North Sea Brent values deflated a portion of the premium LLS holds to benchmark.
Widening Brent-West Texas Intermediate/Cushing spreads also presssured prompt LLS dealings, making it more attractive for moving North Sea grades to the U.S. Gulf.
West Texas Sour/Midland remained unchanged at a $1.40-35 discount to the marker. June WTI/Cushing was talked at $2.00-06.
June exchange for physicals lost some edge, declining around five cents to talk at plus 8-11 cents.
